description:
Found while building #189 (s330). Sibling of the `=~ s///`-on-element bug fixed there.

  my @a = ("abc"); substr($a[0],0,1,"Q");     # perl: Qbc — PCL: abc, SILENT
  my @b = ("abc"); substr($b[0],0,1) = "Z";   # perl: Zbc — PCL: abc, SILENT
  sub s4 { substr($_[0],0,1,"Q") } my $v="abc"; s4($v);   # same

The caller side is already right after #189 ($v IS boxed — _sub_writes_args flags substr/vec/pos on $_[N]); the CALLEE lowers substr's target as a VALUE.

CAUSE: Pl/ExprToCL.pm has %lvalue_funcs = qw(chop chomp undef) — TWO copies (~line 2433 and ~3265), and both omit substr (4-arg), vec, read/sysread/recv. Only names in that table get lvalue_context(1), which is what makes _elem_accessor emit p-aref-box / p-gethash-box instead of p-aref / p-gethash. Same "second copy of a mechanism, both incomplete" shape as #140.

FIX SHAPE: one shared table (rule 11), consumed by both copies; substr only in its 4-arg form and as an assignment target; vec likewise; read/sysread/recv write their buffer argument. Pl::VarAnnotator::arg_writing_builtin (added in s330) is the membership test the #189 scan already uses — route this through it too so the three consumers cannot drift.

WATCH: adding substr blanket-wise also boxes the target of a 3-arg RVALUE substr — measure the corpus-diff before/after and keep the change gated to the writing forms.

=== s543c (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-21, CODE 7ea827a6) ===
VERDICT: NARROWED -- the three filed shapes agree with perl; ONE shape does not, and it is the one a failing row is keyed on.
PASS (= perl): `substr($a[0],0,1,"Q")` -> Qbc; `substr($b[0],0,1) = "Z"` -> Zbc; `sub s4 { substr($_[0],0,1,"Q") } s4($v)` -> Qbc;
  the hash-element and `$r->[0]` twins; `sub s5 { substr($_[0],0,1) = "R" }` -> Rbc; `sub { $_[0] = 'Z' }->(substr($s2,0,1))`
  -> Zbcdef; `w(substr($s3,1,2))` with `sub w { $_[0] = 'YY' }` -> aYYdef.  Fixed by #960 (s463au d3a0b67a: substr / vec / pos
  take their target in perl's loose lvalue context); guarded by Pl/t/lvalue-ref-01.t '#960: substr(ELEM,…) = V and the 4-arg
  call write through' and '#960: a write through an @_ element reaches the caller'.
FAILS (the residue, silent): a substr lvalue passed through @_ under `scalar`:
    my $str = "abcdef"; sub { $_[0] = 'dea' }->( scalar substr $str, 3, 2 ); print "$str\n";
    perl: abcdeaf      PCL: abcdef   (exit 0, nothing on stderr)
  Without the `scalar` the same call writes through, so the suspect is the `scalar` wrapper: it lowers its operand as a VALUE
  and drops the lvalue context the bare substr argument gets.  Cheap discriminating measurement: `./pl2cl` both spellings and
  compare the argument form (the bare one is an lvalue window, the `scalar` one a string).
ROWS keyed on #209: cl/skip-registry.lisp substr.t 'scalar does not affect lvalueness of substr' (:alias) is exactly this
  residue, and its reason text ("the CALLEE lowers substr's target as a value") is out of date -- the callee is right now, the
  `scalar` wrapper is the gap (the registry is under cl/, not edited by s543c).  docs/not-supported.md's '@_ argument aliasing'
  bullet for #209 is corrected to the residue in the s543c commit.  The perl-suite-fails.tsv `#209` cells are TEST NUMBERS.
frequency_reason: a substr lvalue passed through @_ under `scalar` (first pass from the subject, the reviewing session 2026-11-24)
subject: SILENT WRONG: a substr lvalue passed through @_ under `scalar` is not written back -- `sub { $_[0] = "dea" }->(scalar substr $str, 3, 2)` leaves $str (perl-tests/substr.t, the skip-registry row); the element / 4-arg / @_ shapes are fixed (#960)
triage_reason: substr as an lvalue on an element writes nothing -- verify
